title: Product description, quality management approach and product register
blurb: Explain the purpose and key contents of the four management products that support the quality practice.
question: A requirement that every supplier holds a quality policy needs recording. Which management product should hold it?

teach.body: The quality practice relies on four management products: the product description, the quality management approach (part of the PID), and two records in the project log, the quality register and the product register. In plain English: one describes each product and how it will be judged, one explains how the project manages quality overall, and two keep track of checks and of products.

head: Product
Purpose
Where it sits
rows: A product's purpose, composition, derivation, format and quality specifications
Techniques, standards and responsibilities for quality
Summary of all quality activities planned or performed
All products required of a plan and their status

teach.body: A product description sets out a product's purpose, composition, derivation (what it is built from), format and quality specifications: the functional and non-functional requirements with their measures. It also names the quality method, the tolerance, the skills needed and the quality and sustainability responsibilities: who produces, who reviews and who approves. Product descriptions are written for products at every level of plan, by the project manager with input from team managers and specialists.

teach.h: Project product description vs product description

teach.body: The quality management approach describes the quality techniques and standards to be applied, and the roles and responsibilities for achieving the required quality specifications and acceptance criteria. It is agreed in initiation, approved by the board, and forms part of the PID. Project-wide requirements, such as every supplier holding a quality policy, belong here rather than in a single product description.

head: Heading
Example content
rows: The business's or supplier's quality management system
Who plans and controls quality; assurance; acceptance authorities
Legal rules for all outputs; format of the quality register
teach.caption: Practitioner matching questions ask which heading a statement belongs under.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a museum audio guide
teach.body: Thornbury Museums is producing an audio guide. Project manager Elif Kaya records in the quality management approach that all scripts must meet the museum's accessibility standard and that the head of learning is the acceptance authority. The product description for the gallery script specifies 90 seconds per stop, plus or minus ten. When the script passes its review, project support logs the result in the quality register, and the product register shows the script as approved.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) Quality register = quality activities and results; product register = products and their status. (2) The PROJECT product description holds expectations and acceptance criteria; each product description holds quality specifications. (3) Standards that apply to all outputs go in the quality management approach, not in one product's description.

items: Product description: purpose, composition, derivation, format, quality specifications, method, responsibilities.
QMA (PID): techniques, standards and responsibilities; headings references, responsibilities, tools and techniques, standards.
Quality register: all quality activities planned or performed; used by PM and project assurance.
Product register: all products of a plan and their status; closed in closing a project.

summary: You can now explain the purpose and key contents of the product description, quality management approach, quality register and product register. You can also decide which product or heading a piece of quality information belongs in.

A.q: What is the purpose of the product register?
options: To summarize all quality activities planned or performed
To list all products required of a plan and their status
To describe the quality standards for the project
To record the project's major products and acceptance criteria
A.why: The product register lists all products required of a plan and the status of those products (manual 8.5).

whyNot.0: This is the purpose of the quality register.
whyNot.2: Quality standards are described in the quality management approach.
whyNot.3: The project product description holds the major products and acceptance criteria.

A.q: Which management product describes the quality techniques and standards to be applied and the roles and responsibilities for achieving the required quality?
A.why: The quality management approach describes the quality techniques and standards to be applied and the roles and responsibilities for achieving the required quality specifications and acceptance criteria.

whyNot.0: A product description covers one product's purpose, composition, derivation, format and quality specifications.
whyNot.1: The quality register records quality activities and their results.
whyNot.2: The PPD holds the user's quality expectations and acceptance criteria.

A.q: Which of these is part of a product description?
A.why: A product description sets out a product's purpose, composition, derivation (where it comes from), format and quality specifications.

whyNot.1: Stage cost tolerance is in the stage plan, set by the board.
whyNot.2: Risk appetite is the business's attitude to risk, reflected in the risk management approach.
whyNot.3: Reporting frequency is a progress control in the PID.

B.q: A council requires every supplier on the project to hold a recognized quality policy. Where should this be documented?
B.why: The quality management approach describes the quality standards and procedures to be followed across the project, so a requirement for all suppliers belongs there.

whyNot.1: Product descriptions cover individual products, not requirements on all suppliers.
whyNot.2: The quality register records quality activities and their results.
whyNot.3: The product register lists products and their status.

B.q: A housing association's project will issue many forms to tenants. Under which heading of the quality management approach should 'every form issued to tenants must comply with data protection legislation' be recorded?
B.why: The standards heading covers standards that apply to quality management across the project, such as a legal requirement that applies to every output of a given kind, not just one product (manual 8.5).

whyNot.0: References point to associated documents, such as the business's quality management system.
whyNot.1: Responsibilities define who plans, controls, assures and accepts.
whyNot.3: Supporting tools and techniques cover methods such as testing, inspection and prototyping.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. The quality register is part of the project log.
2. The product register lists quality check results.
3. Product descriptions include quality responsibilities such as approvers.
4. The quality management approach is part of the project log.
B.why: The quality register sits in the project log (1), and product descriptions include quality and sustainability responsibilities such as who approves (3).

whyNot.1: Statement 2 is false: check results go in the quality register; the product register lists products and their status.
whyNot.2: Both are false: the product register lists products, and the QMA is part of the PID.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the QMA is part of the PID, not the project log.

C.q: After a usability trial of a booking app, a team member writes: 'Failed: users completed 3 of 5 tasks; retrial booked once fixes are made.' Which management product and which heading should hold this?
C.why: The quality register records each quality activity, and its result heading shows whether the product passed or failed and the response to a failure (manual 8.5).

whyNot.0: Specifications define what the product must meet, not the outcome of a check on it.
whyNot.1: The QMA defines responsibilities in advance; it does not record individual checks.
whyNot.2: The product register tracks product status, not the outcome of a quality activity.

C.q: The checkout page of a theatre's new booking app must load within 2 seconds. Which management product and which part should hold this?
C.why: Quality specifications in a product description give the functional and non-functional requirements of that product with their measures (manual 8.5).

whyNot.0: Standards in the QMA apply across the project, not to one product's measures.
whyNot.2: The PPD describes the project product as a whole at a high level, not one page's measures.
whyNot.3: The quality register records activities and results, not requirements.

C.q: In which process is the product register closed, and which practice uses it to confirm the final stage's products were delivered?
C.why: In closing a project, the plans practice checks the product register to confirm the final stage's products have been delivered, and the register is then closed.

whyNot.0: The register is not closed at a stage boundary; it carries on into the next stage.
whyNot.2: The register is maintained during controlling a stage, not closed.
whyNot.3: The issues practice deals with the issue register, not the product register.

reteach.title: A recipe book and a kitchen whiteboard
reteach.question: How does a busy restaurant keep track of dishes and checks?

blocks.body: Each dish has a recipe card: what it is for, its ingredients, how it is plated and how the chef will judge it (product description). The kitchen rulebook covers hygiene standards and who signs dishes off (quality management approach). One whiteboard logs every taste test and its result (quality register). Another lists every dish on tonight's menu and whether it is prepped, cooking or served (product register).

blocks.text: The taste-test log and the dish status board are different boards. So are the quality and product registers.

explain.body: Purpose, composition, derivation, format and quality specifications, plus method, tolerance, skills and responsibilities.

test.q: What does the 'derivation' heading of a product description record?
options: What the product is built from
test.why: Derivation describes where the product comes from: its source products or inputs.

whyNot.0: Approvers are part of the quality responsibilities.
whyNot.2: Test dates are recorded in the quality register.
whyNot.3: Costs are in plans and work packages.

explain.body: Part of the PID: techniques, standards and responsibilities for achieving the required quality.

test.q: Of which management product is the quality management approach a part?
test.why: The quality management approach is one of the management approaches in the PID.

whyNot.0: The project log holds the quality and product registers, not the QMA.
whyNot.1: The brief is assembled in starting up, before the approaches are agreed in initiation.
whyNot.3: A stage plan describes one stage's products and work.

explain.body: Summarizes all quality activities planned or performed; used by the PM and project assurance to review progress.

test.q: Which heading would you expect in the quality register?
test.why: The quality register records the result of each quality activity, with its method, dates and responsibilities.

whyNot.0: Composition is a product description heading.
whyNot.1: Proximity is a risk register heading.
whyNot.3: Derivation is a product description heading.

explain.body: Lists all products required of a plan and their status; checked and closed in closing a project.

test.q: Which record would show that a training manual is still in progress?
test.why: The product register lists all products required of a plan and their status.

whyNot.0: The quality register records quality activities and results, not product status.
whyNot.1: The daily log holds informal issues and notes.
